transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, well, my family actually asked me to come in. It's mostly about... well, it's about my father's death. 

I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But I look at data for a living, and when I actually compare the timestamps, the missing attachments... and just the way certain community members completely avoid my questions when I bring it up... it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. I'm just trying to get to the bottom of it, but it's causing some friction with my family, so... here I am.
Aside from these concerns about your father, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

No, definitely not. I don't hear voices or anything like that. My hearing is perfectly fine, and I've never experienced anything where I'm hearing things that aren't there or that other people can't hear. It's really just the inconsistencies in the data and the records that I'm focused on.

If you were presented with definitive, verifiable proof from an independent third party that the hospital records were indeed accurate and no information was hidden, would you be willing to reconsider your conclusion?

I suppose I would be willing to look at it, but... I'd have a really hard time just accepting it. 

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. But like I said, I analyze systems for a living. When I compare the timestamps myself, and look at the missing attachments... and then factor in the way certain community members completely avoid my questions when I bring those things up... it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death. 

So, an independent party can say whatever they want, but they would have to explain the actual discrepancies I'm already looking right at. Until then, the data is what it is.
Do you feel as though there are people or organizations specifically monitoring your movements or trying to interfere with your daily life beyond this situation with your father's records?

No, not at all. I mean, nobody's following me or tapping my phone or anything like that, if that's what you're asking. My daily life is pretty normal. I go to work, do my job, come home. 

There's no big conspiracy against me personally. It's really just... strictly about getting to the truth with my dad's case. Outside of trying to get answers about those specific files, nobody is bothering me, and I definitely don't feel like I'm being watched or monitored.
Has this situation with your father's records impacted your ability to perform your job duties or maintain your relationships with your family members?

At work, no, it hasn't really affected me. My job performance has stayed pretty steady. I can still focus on my systems analysis and get my work done just fine. 

But with my family... well, it's caused a bit of friction. Some of my relatives have started avoiding conversations with me. I think it's because they know I might bring up the hospital records and what I believe was concealed about my dad. They just don't want to talk about it, so they kind of distance themselves.
Do you believe that the people avoiding your questions are doing so because they are intentionally conspiring to keep the truth about your father from being discovered?

I don't know if I'd use the word "conspiring," exactly. That makes it sound like some big movie plot. 

I just think... they know something isn't right, or maybe they've been told not to talk about certain details, and they're just choosing to look the other way. It's easier for them to avoid me than to look at the data and admit that the hospital didn't tell us the whole truth. So, I don't think my family is actively plotting against me, they're just... keeping their heads down. But the people at the hospital or the community board who are dodging my questions? Yeah, I think they know exactly what they're hiding.
Are there any other topics or situations in your life where you feel you have uncovered information or patterns that others around you fail to see or refuse to acknowledge?

No, not really. I mean, my job is literally about finding patterns in data and fixing system errors, so I'm used to noticing things at work that other people might miss. But that's just professional. Outside of work and this situation with my dad's hospital records... no. I don't have any other big theories or anything. Everything else in my life is pretty straightforward. It's really just this one specific issue with the hospital that I'm focused on.
Does the amount of time you spend investigating these records or thinking about the hospital's actions interfere with your ability to enjoy your hobbies, sleep, or take care of your basic needs?

No, it doesn't really interfere with any of that. I mean, I still go to work every day, handle my projects, pay my bills... I keep my normal routine. I still get enough sleep and take care of myself. 

Like I said before, the main place things get tense is just when I bring up my questions about the records with my family or the community board members. That's where the friction is. But it hasn't taken over my whole life or stopped me from functioning normally.
